newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures eye France, Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures eye France, Bundesbank.

text.p: German Bunds and futures traded firmer in early dealings on Wednesday in a modest recovery from unsettling activity on Tuesday despite ongoing worries about the fate of European currency union.
DTB June Bund futures were up nine basis points at 100.90 points, while the benchmark 10-year Bund due July 2007 was at 100.72 percent compared with the close on Tuesday at 100.57.

Concerns about the start date of European monetary union, spurred by worries about the outcome of Sunday's French run-off election, still weighed on Bund prices as traders said they expected volatile movements during the session.

"The uncertainities surrounding the French election situation and the conflicting forces for Germany that surrounds it make the outlook clearly more random than usual," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Futures & Options said in a market commentary.
"However, if prices could break the top of the recent down channels, then technical factors would start to provide bullish momentum instead of bearish impulses," Deutsche said.
Market attention also focused on the Bundesbank meeting.
The German central bank council was scheduled to meet a day earlier than usual on Wednesday for its fortnightly policy meeting due to Thursday's regional German holiday.
No official interest rate change was expected.

The market instead focused on the council's plans to discuss Germany's plans to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves. Bonn sources said the Bundesbank was expected to approve the plan, considered to be relatively conservative.
It was unclear whether any official statement will be made by the Bundesbank after the council meeting meeting.

Bonn sources said late on Tuesday the plan to revalue the Bundesbank gold reserves, a bid to help plug Germany's debt to meet EMU entry criteria, could boost federal finances by an extra 10 to 12 billion marks in both 1997 and 1998.

If the gold plan is approved, and the left-wing wins Sunday's French election, traders said the results could open up the prospect of a less strict interpretation of entry guidelines for currency union, slated to start in January 1999.
"The market is still short-term bullish but people are getting nervous about the French election," one trader said.
On a technical basis, DTB June Bund futures were expected to face resistance at 100.97 and 101.15, while support was evident at 100.66 and 100.54.
